text:
sam: Quick heads-up — ran another reserved capacity vs hosted demand pass for next quarter. If traffic follows the new marketing curve we get a 23% idle on our US pool by May unless we reassign commits or throttle burst.

lia: Ugh, that would be a lot of wasted spend. Do you have the per-region breakdown?

sam: Pasted quick numbers (util% = reserved used / reserved total):
```
region, reserved_gpus, expected_peak_used, util%
us-west1, 200, 150, 75%
us-east1, 120, 80, 67%
eu-west1, 80, 40, 50%
ap-southeast1, 40, 35, 88%
```
This assumes hosted API traffic + typical dedicated steady usage. The riskiest is eu-west1 and us-east1.

marco: Is eu-west1 low because of fewer customers or because we pin hosted traffic to regional replicas? We could do cross-region spill to us-east if latency allows.

sam: It's partly both — hosted traffic ties to customer location for compliance but for many requests we can route to a compatible model in us-east with <30ms added p50. We need to check SLO/latency impact.

tara: Finance flagged the last invoice: there are unused committed discounts still being charged as 'sustained usage' instead of 'reservations' in one line item. @finance-bot any notes? :eyes: 

finance-bot: Noted: billing shows a misapplied discount for GCP committed use from invoice 2026-02. Finance will open a ticket with GCP; estimated recoverable credit ~ $18k.

lia: Great — that helps the shortfall. For capacity decisions, can we model a 3-month runway metric: months until committed spend > projected usage by X%?

sam: I ran a tiny script and got runway months with conservative growth:
```
commit_total_monthly = 0.75 * current_reserved_cost
projected_consumption = baseline + marketing_growth
runway_months = commit_budget / (commit_total_monthly - projected_consumption)
```
Current quick estimate: runway=4 months at current plan before we start paying pure waste.

marco: Options: 1) Try to modify reservations with cloud provider for flexible sizing (negotiation), 2) Rebalance reserved GPUs across regions, 3) Convert some to spot for burst and rely on burst pool, 4) Delay new model rollouts.

tara: Also consider reducing default session length on hosted API (2 mins -> 90s) for non-interactive calls. Small change but reduces avg sequence length and can cut tokens/GPU time.

lia: Can we auto-scale dedicated pools more aggressively to absorb hosted spikes so reserved stays for baseline? Or is that the opposite problem?

sam: Dedicated pools are on separate bills for customers with commits — can't use them for hosted. But we do have a shared "burst" pool funded from reserved overflow (the one costing us). We can tighten burst budget and fallback to quantized smaller models when burst budget is exhausted.

ops-bot: Automated utilization report generated: /reports/reservations/2026-03-07. Attachment: 1778201123-res-util.csv

marco: I'll prototype a routing policy that will: prefer local region until util <85% else route to us-east, and fall back to 8-bit quant model at util >95%. Should be low-risk.

sam: Sounds good. Action items:
- marco: drop PR with routing policy + traffic test by Wed (1778330000)
- lia: update runway calc in spreadsheet and include invoice credit when confirmed
- tara: propose short token-limited config change for hosted API and measure perf
- finance: follow up GCP ticket and confirm credit amount

lia: One more ask — can we add a simple chart to console showing "reserved utilization runway" per region? That'd make QBR conversations much easier.

sam: Agree. I'll file a console ticket after we confirm the model. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

finance-bot: Ticket created: FIN-4231 (GCP refund claim). Estimated follow-up 3-7 business days.

ops-bot: Note: scheduled maintenance for us-east1 GPUs next week could reduce available burst capacity by ~10% during the window. Recommend factoring that into Wednesday's traffic test.

tara: Good catch. I'll schedule the hosted traffic test outside the maintenance window.

marco: If we need a hot config check before Wed ping me and I'll stand by for an emergency rollback.

sam: Closing here for now. Will post results of the routing test and updated runway calc in this thread.
